sermon.title: Does the Gospel Favor Financially Poor People? 02/25/2018
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: Pastor David G. Kincer asks whether the gospel favors the financially poor and answers that Jesus meant the poor in spirit. God looks on the contrite who tremble at his word. Everyone can be rich in the word of Christ, in wisdom from above and in the Holy Spirit, and worship is the followers’ time to minister to one another.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added from the speaker’s pauses and then corrected by hand, and obvious caption errors (names, Bible references) were fixed; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor notes: Kept as spoken: “Romans 10 11” (generosity is 10:12); “Matthew 3:13 3:11.” Points to check: 3.2 billion people living on $2.50 a day, 70% on under $10 a day, 85% literacy, 95% never own a car, travel or fly (1:00–3:00); “13 tribes” of Israel; 15 languages at Pentecost. Sensitive content kept as spoken: Muslims and many Christians believe they are “the dominant nation”; disagreement with Christians who expect a rebuilt temple; ministers named (Oral Roberts, Billy Graham, Norman Vincent Peale “very questionable,” Martin Luther King, Jesse Jackson, Jerry Falwell, Joyce Meyer, Jakes, Schuller) (24:09); “tongues are not for today … a bunch of baloney.”

faqs.question: What did Jesus say about the poor?
faqs.answer: You will always have them with you.

faqs.question: How did Jesus prove he was the coming one?
faqs.answer: Miracles and the gospel preached to the poor.

faqs.question: Whom does God look on in Isaiah 66:2?
faqs.answer: The contrite who tremble at his word.

faqs.question: What should dwell in us richly?
Who should ask God for wisdom?
What happened as Jesus opened the scriptures?
What did they hear at Pentecost?
faqs.answer: A sound like a mighty rushing wind.
